source.creator: Bram Stoker
source.basis: Stoker's novel: a tall, pale nobleman in black who can change into a bat; caped vampire costume is a long-standing stage convention. Not based on any film likeness (no medallion, no Lugosi features).
source.notice: Based on Bram Stoker's novel "Dracula" (1897) — public domain.

source.creator: F. W. Murnau (director); Max Schreck (Count Orlok)
source.basis: The film's famous shot of Count Orlok's shadow creeping up the staircase: bald head, pointed ears, hunched back and long clawed fingers, in sepia film tint with projector flicker.
source.notice: Based on the 1922 film "Nosferatu" — public domain in the US (published 1922) and the EU (director, writer and composer all died more than 70 years ago).

source.creator: Mary Shelley
source.basis: Shelley's description: yellow skin, lustrous flowing black hair, watery yellowish eyes in dun-white sockets, straight black lips, stitched-together features, brought to life by a spark in a storm. Deliberately avoids the Universal/Karloff make-up (no flat-top head, no neck bolts, no green skin).
source.notice: Based on Mary Shelley's novel "Frankenstein" (1818) — public domain.

source.creator: Washington Irving
source.basis: Irving's tale: a headless Hessian rider in a flowing cloak on a huge black horse, who hurls his 'head' (a pumpkin) at Ichabod Crane; the blazing jack-o'-lantern follows folk tradition.
source.notice: Based on Washington Irving's "The Legend of Sleepy Hollow" (1820) — public domain.

source.creator: Ancient Greek tradition (Hesiod, Ovid)
source.basis: The Gorgon of Greek myth with living snakes for hair whose gaze turns onlookers to stone; generic classical depiction.
source.notice: Based on the ancient Greek myth of Medusa — public domain.

source.creator: Traditional European folklore and heraldry
source.basis: Generic fire-breathing dragon of medieval legend and heraldry (horns, green scales, pale belly plates, flame breath).
source.notice: Based on traditional dragon folklore — public domain.

source.creator: Ancient Greek, Egyptian and later traditions (Herodotus, Ovid)
source.basis: The mythical firebird that bursts into flame and is reborn from its own ashes; generic heraldic phoenix with spread wings.
source.notice: Based on the ancient phoenix myth — public domain.

source.creator: Ancient and medieval European tradition (Ctesias, medieval bestiaries)
source.basis: Generic white horse with a single spiralled golden horn from legend and bestiaries; the rainbow is a decorative flourish.
source.notice: Based on the unicorn of legend — public domain.

source.creator: Scandinavian folklore (recorded by Erik Pontoppidan, 1752)
source.basis: The giant tentacled sea monster of Norwegian legend that drags sailing ships beneath the waves.
source.notice: Based on the Scandinavian legend of the Kraken — public domain.

source.creator: Popular folklore; early fiction such as Jane Loudon's "The Mummy!" (1827)
source.basis: Generic linen-wrapped Egyptian mummy with glowing eyes and outstretched arms; not based on any film character or actor likeness.
source.notice: Based on the folklore of the walking Egyptian mummy — public domain.

source.creator: European folklore (lycanthropy legends from antiquity onward)
source.basis: Folklore of a man who turns into a wolf under the full moon, shown as a silhouette against the moon; not based on any film design.
source.notice: Based on European werewolf folklore — public domain.

source.creator: Folk tradition (shrouded spirit imagery, 18th-19th century)
source.basis: The classic white-sheet ghost with eye holes and a wavy hem, derived from burial-shroud folklore.
source.notice: Based on the traditional sheet-ghost of folklore — public domain.

source.creator: Himalayan (Sherpa) folklore
source.basis: The shaggy white ape-like snow creature of Himalayan legend, beating its chest and roaring in falling snow.
source.notice: Based on Himalayan Yeti folklore — public domain.

source.creator: Scottish folklore (first recorded in Adomnán's Life of St Columba)
source.basis: Generic long-necked lake creature with humps rising from a Highland loch; not based on any specific photograph.
source.notice: Based on the Scottish legend of the Loch Ness Monster — public domain.

source.creator: Traditional tales; Aladdin first published by Antoine Galland (1704-1717)
source.basis: The jinn who emerges as smoke from an oil lamp when it is rubbed; drawn as a lilac smoke figure with crossed arms and a smoke tail — not the blue Disney character.
source.notice: Based on "One Thousand and One Nights" (Aladdin, Galland 1710) — public domain.

source.creator: Homer (Odyssey) and Virgil (Aeneid)
source.basis: The giant wooden horse on wheels that hid Greek soldiers (crested helmets) inside, from the Trojan War legend.
source.notice: Based on the Trojan War legend in Homer and Virgil — public domain.

source.creator: Irish folk tradition
source.basis: The carved lantern of the Irish legend of Stingy Jack, carried to light his way; drawn as a candle-lit carved pumpkin with flickering glow.
source.notice: Based on the Irish folk tale of Stingy Jack and the jack-o'-lantern tradition — public domain.
